title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII close: double mode of existing from conception via hypostatic union — stop before §.XXIV
pass_a_gloss: Nay in Num. 5 he proves from 1 Cor. 15 that this double Mode of Christ’s Body existing belonged to it no less before than after the resurrection. On the Spiritual mode of existing from the very conception of Christ’s body he pronounces thus: Not from some virtue of the Resurrection did Christ, but from the beginning, by the force of His hypostatic Union, bring the body’s own Spirituality with Him into the Blessed Virgin’s womb. For if it had been otherwise, the Apostle would incongruously — or at least less aptly — after prefacing that citation of Gen. 2:7 ‘the first man Adam was made into a living soul’ subjoin also this (as if answering what was already said, so that to some it even seems cited): ‘The last Adam was made into a life-giving spirit,’ 1 Cor. 15:45. But the first Adam from the very beginning of his creation was made into a living soul. What parity then, what symphony or Correspondence, will there be, unless the second Adam also was made into a life-giving spirit from the very moment of His conception? p. 331 near the end.
pass_b_english: §.XXIII close (n. 5): the body’s double mode of existing belonged before the resurrection no less than after — spirituality of the body brought from the beginning by hypostatic union into the Virgin’s womb, not first from resurrection power (1 Cor. 15 with Gen. 2:7).
Else Adam’s living-soul / last-Adam life-giving-spirit correspondence fails unless the second Adam was so from conception’s moment. Stop before §.XXIV.
source_text: Quin Num. 5tô. Duplicem hunc existendi Corporis Christi Modum, non minùs ante, quàm post resurrectionem, isti competiisse, evincit ex 1. Cor. 15. De Spirituali existendi modo, ab ipsâ inde corporis Christi conceptione, ita pronuncians: Non ex aliqua virtute Resurrectionis Christus, sed inde à principio, per vim hypostaticæ suæ Unionis, Spiritualitatem corporis ipsam, secum attulisse in uterum B. Virginis. Aliter enim si fuisset, incongruè satis saltem minùs appositè, ab Apostolo, citationem illam præmittente Gen. 2, 7. factus est primus Homo Adam in animam viventem, subjungitur & hoc (quasi quod priùs jam dicto sic respondeat, ut & citi quoque, nonnullis videatur) Factus est novissimus Adam in spiritum vivificantem 1. Cor 15, 45. Primus autem Adam, ab ipso primordio condituræ suæ, in animam viventem factus est. Quæ igitur jam paritas, quæ symphōnēsis aut Correspondentia erit, nisi & secundus Adam in spiritum vivificantem, ab ipso quoque conceptionis suæ momento, ita factus fuerit? p. 331. circa finem.

lemmas.gloss: by the force of hypostatic Union

notes: §.XXIII close: double mode from conception; before §.XXIV.
